# Fine-Grained Complexity

This course studies more precise complexity classifications than the usual polynomial-time versus NP-hard distinction. It develops conditional lower bounds from conjectures about core problems and combinatorial reductions between them, motivated by the practical differences between near-linear, quadratic, and larger running times. Topics include k-SAT, 3-SUM, All-Pairs Shortest Paths, k-Clique, fine-grained results for string, graph, and geometric problems (including Edit Distance, Diameter, and Closest Pair), hardness of approximation, parameterized complexity, and barriers for reductions.

The `lecture-notes` skill (`shared/.github/skills/lecture-notes/SKILL.md`) has the full workflow for reading handwritten lecture notes.
